(734) 752-9667
Twitter: @anthonyfenech
From: Jahnke, James <jjahnke@freepress.com>
Sent: Friday, June 19, 2015 1:59 PM
To: Myers, Gene <gmyers@freepress.com>; Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>
Subject: RE: FRIDAY-FOR-SATURDAY 
 
Yep, Gene nailed it. The two things you can do to separate yourself:
1.       Speed on the things everyone is going to have.
2.       Doing things that other people won’t have. Scoops and analyzing hot topics.
That’s how to drive ye olde traffic!!

From: Myers, Gene 
Sent: Friday, June 19, 2015 12:28 PM
To: Fenech, Anthony
Cc: Jahnke, James
Subject: RE: FRIDAY-FOR-SATURDAY
ANTHONY: I’m going to throw out a few ideas, and ask James to contribute his thoughts. But first … a couple other points.

Again, pageviews aren’t everything (although they are important). You score high with you podcast and your postgame analysis videos (and any videos of players), and that’s important for engagement time, which is super important. You also do well on Twitter, of course.
1) Be the first to post on news. Don’t need big (or complete) stories. Just 3-4-5 graphs. Then update. Take JV news, for instance.

2) Think like a fan. Many are worried about Soria. So many homers and bad outings lately. Fans fear he will be the next Nathan or Papa Grande. You could have written a sider about Soria after the grand slam that points out the trend.

3) More analysis. Take a look the past few days at Birkett’s daily observations after each day of the minicamp. http://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2015/06/18/detroit-lions-minicamp-thoughts/28930271/ http://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2015/06/17/lions-dime-defense/28887561/ Analysis doesn’t need to be long. In fact, it’s often better short. Folks look for your view and opinion. You do that in the podcast and the videos. Incorporate it into print.

From: Fenech, Anthony 
Sent: Friday, June 19, 2015 9:39 AM
To: Myers, Gene
Subject: Re: FRIDAY-FOR-SATURDAY
Why are my numbers so low?

From: Myers, Gene
Sent: Thursday, June 18, 2015 10:57 PM
To: Birkett, David; Brudenell, Mike; Bull, Kevin; Collison, Bill; Crawford, Kirkland; Darby, David; delaGarza, Marisela; Ellis, Vince; Farrell, Perry; Fenech, Anthony; Ford, Ryan; Jahnke, James; Manzullo, Brian; Marcinkoski, Tim; McCabe, Mick; Monarrez, Carlos; Rexrode, Joe; St. James, Helene; Schrader, Steve; Sharp, Drew; Seidel, Jeff; Sipple, George; Snider, Lee; Snyder, Mark; Tarsha, Jeff; Visconti, Joy; Weber, Jessica; Windsor, Shawn; Itchue, Michael; Robles Hernandez, Dora; Myers, Gene
Cc: Gene Myers; Ldelves22@yahoo.com; Beth Myers (myersbg@comcast.net)
Subject: FRIDAY-FOR-SATURDAY
Gene here with the early line on the Friday plan … from his Canton lair.

1) OK … here’s this week’s heavy-duty vacation lineup: Bill (until Sunday), Joe (until Monday), Steve (until Wednesday), Mark (until next Friday), Aussie Mike (until June 29), Kevin (until June 30) and Mick (until next month). Lee returns Friday.
2) Mari will be the day editor and arrive at 3:30 p.m. She also will help edit Sunday copy later in her shift. Kevin starts his long vacation. David will work on the Sunday sections.

3) As for yours truly, I should arrive by late morning. James and I will watch the shop until Mari’s arrival. I have a slew of weekend duties, including setting Sunday-for-Monday and Monday-for-Tuesday.
4) Here’s the web lineup: Webmizz at 5 a.m., James at 8 a.m., Brian at 1:30 p.m. and Mike at 7 p.m.
5) For Saturday’s print editions, our space is pretty much right on the mark. So … if you have an extra story, please alert Gene ASAP.
6) Check out the attached tentative budget. And Ryan’s front page.

7) UPDATE: Talked at length with George on Thursday. As per his father’s wishes, there will be no services. A few details remain, but George likely will say that in lieu of flowers he would appreciate donations to gotbeagles.com, a rescue organization for beagles, which his dad loved. George will return to duty Monday.

8) FUN WITH METRICS: We’re gonna look at a slice of  our metrics from Wednesday. Our desktop numbers outpaced our mobile numbers (246,169 vs. 212,824) for stories. Here’s a look at the day’s pageview leaders:

9) EVERYBODY NEEDS AN EDITOR! We all hate corrections. Check out the mistake that a yoga studio outside Ocean City, N.J. – my annual July vacation lair – made in an e-mail announcing its summer schedule. And I had thought it was a new style of yoga – Tony Soprano Yoga or Real Housewives of New Jersey Yoga.

Easy Does It BackhandingSunday, July 5, 11:15-1:15w/Natalie Levin   What would it be like to spend two luxurious hours opening up the spine and muscles surrounding it?  We will use blocks and straps to help open the back body and will incorporate some flowing movements as well! More info and to register:www.njyogazone.com$30 in advance

Thanks to all those who let us know that we misspelled "Backbending".  Though we'd love to blame it on autocorrect, it was probably user error! Easy Does It BackbendingSunday, July 5, 11:15-1:15w/Natalie Levin  What would it be like to spend two luxurious hours opening up the spine and muscles surrounding it?  We will use blocks and straps to help open the back body and will incorporate some flowing movements as well! More info and to register:www.njyogazone.com$30 in advance

10) PUSH THOSE APPS! If you write a story or column about the Tigers or Lions – or edit a piece about these same feline teams – please add one of these sentences in the tagline: Download our free Tigers Xtra app on your Apple and Android devices. Download our free Lions Xtra app on your Apple and Android devices.

11) For today’s attached photo … It’s my run-in with Quicken Loans security. About 9:30 Thursday morning, I parked on the empty top floor of the Financial District Garage, which, of course, is across the street from the federal courthouse. On the roof was our good buddy Stephen Mounteer, who was testing our the Free Press’ satellite phone. I stopped to talk with him. He joked that his activities might be considered suspicious or curious by courthouse security. And a few minutes later a security guard on a mountain bike paid us and visit to find out what we were up to. He was very nice, told us he worked for Quicken. I asked what he was ordered to check out, and he replied: “We had a report of a man with suspicious device and another with a backpack on the roof.” We showed our IDs, Steve finished his work and I talked with the guard about his bike (it was a sweet Giant).
Websters: Webmizz early morning (5:00), James morning (8:00), Brian day (1:30) and Mike night (7:00).
Notes: David will work on the Sunday section. Kevin will be on vacation until June 30.
Your text assignments (some ending in 0620) should arrive Thursday night from the Text Assignment Elf (in this case Jessica).
Pistons p2 update (10-12), please file by 4 p.m.
POSSIBLE Pistons draft update (13), please file by 4 p.m.
NOTE: If a big-name prospect comes to town, we could the additional story.
Tigers p2 update (8-12), please file by 7:05 p.m.
Tigers V-Mart column (18), please file by 8:30 p.m.
NOTE: Add 1-2 graphs how V-Mart fared in game by 10:15 p.m.
Tigers gamer (13), please file near final out.
NOTE II: If game isn’t going to end by 10:30 p.m., please file a game story by then that the desk can update on deadline.
Tigers sub gamer (15-18), please file within two hours of final out.
Tigers sub V-Mart column (20), please file within two hours of final out.
NOTE III: Could be a few tweaks, just an add of postgame quotes or a complete rewrite.
Lions p2 update (6-10), please file by 5 p.m.
Wings p2 update (10-12), please file by 6:30 p.m.
Wolverines p2 update (8-10), already in the house.
Spartans p2 update (8-10), it comes when it comes or already in the house.
